one_liner: AI workflows that cut admin hours for small accounting firms, sold as a monthly retainer.
example: Illustrative example: the board, buyer and market results are invented to show the format.

glance.problem: Small accounting firms lose hours every week to client intake, document chasing and follow-up emails.
glance.customer: Owners of accounting firms with 3 to 20 staff.
glance.offer: Done-for-you AI automations for intake, documents and follow-ups, maintained every month.

assumptions: the founder works solo at first
firms already use cloud accounting software

board.reason: A painful, expensive problem, but the offer sells setup work, not a guaranteed outcome.
board.recommendation: Sell a result: 10 admin hours saved a week, or the next month is free.
board.quote: Make people an offer so good they would feel stupid saying no.

board.reason: Many freelancers sell the same tools; nothing yet stops a copycat.
board.recommendation: Own one niche completely: accounting firms only, with their exact workflows.

board.reason: Demand is plausible, but the founder is not yet a known name among firm owners.
board.recommendation: Publish one case study a month and speak at local accountants' meetups.
board.quote: Pitch, Publish, Product, Profile and Partnerships

board.reason: Today it is the founder's hours; it only compounds if the know-how becomes a product.
board.recommendation: Turn the three most common workflows into a packaged template product.
board.quote: You're not going to get rich renting out your time.

board.reason: The downside is small: low startup cost, a job kept, and paying customers early.
board.recommendation: List the three ways this fails, starting with a data-security incident, and prevent each.

strengths: A real, costly pain: admin hours
Low startup cost, paid from the first client
The founder knows accounting firms from the inside

risks.risk: Accounting software vendors build the same automations in.
A client-data security incident ends trust overnight.
Easy to copy: any freelancer can learn the same tools.

objections: $2,500 a month is a lot for a small firm
My software may do this next year
flip: Proof from a firm like mine

voices.says: If it saves my team a day a week, I'd pay. Show me first.
Security is my first question, not the last.

competitors.name: Generalist automation agencies
competitors.what: Automate any business, not accounting specifically

competitors.name: Do-it-yourself tools
competitors.what: Automation platforms the firm sets up itself

competitors.name: Accounting software add-ons
competitors.what: Built-in features from the firms' own software

market.gap: Nobody specializes in small accounting firms with maintained, done-for-you workflows and a security promise.

questions: Which single workflow would a firm pay for first?
How could we guarantee the result, not just the work?
What would make us hard to copy in 12 months?
How do we answer the security question before it is asked?
Could the know-how become a product that sells without our hours?
Who are the first five firms we could call this week?

tests.test: Call 10 firm owners about their most painful admin task
tests.success: At least 6 name the same task

tests.test: Offer a one-month paid pilot to 5 firms
